faq.a: Luciferin is the chemical fuel that glows in fireflies and many other glowing creatures. The name comes from the Latin lucifer, meaning light-bringer.

faq.q: How do fireflies switch their light on and off?
faq.a: Fireflies control the oxygen reaching their light cells. A nerve signal releases a gas called nitric oxide that lets oxygen in, the reaction runs, and the lantern flashes.
asks: How do fireflies control their flashes?

faq.q: Why is firefly light called cold light?
faq.a: Almost all the energy of the reaction comes out as light, with very little heat. An old filament bulb, by contrast, wastes most of its energy as heat, which is why it gets hot.
Mostly to find a mate. Each species has its own flash pattern, a bit like a secret code, and females answer males of their own kind. The glow also warns predators that fireflies taste bad.
asks: Why do fireflies glow at night?

faq.a: No, fireflies are beetles. They are sometimes called lightning bugs, and there are about two thousand species around the world.
asks: What kind of insect is a firefly?
Are glow-worms the same as fireflies?

facts: Fireflies are beetles, and there are around 2,000 known species.
Firefly light is made by the enzyme luciferase acting on luciferin with oxygen and ATP.
Each firefly species has its own flash pattern for finding mates.

quiz.say: What does a firefly control to switch its light on and off?
quiz.show: A firefly turns its glow on by letting in…
quiz.why: The light reaction needs oxygen, so the firefly flashes by letting oxygen reach its light cells.

wrong.1: Fireflies make their own light chemically; they do not store sunlight.
wrong.2: Water is not what switches the reaction on.
